issues: This is seventeenth-century source medicine. None of its natal illness, longevity, anatomy, psychiatric, speech, sight or fertility assertions are clinically validated or applicable to a real patient.
The original five health significator categories and three factors must be considered together; selecting one after a medical history is seen is retrospective fitting.
Lilly distinguishes a disease significator from the author or cause of an illness; the latter is a speculative astrological label, not verified medical causation.
The author claims severity grows with two afflictions, exact aspects and angular malefics, but gives no clinical measurement or calibrated likelihood.
A single source first-edition planet table is represented by two cells per planet (body parts and historical ailments); the 150 normalized list terms are NOT 150 independent cases.
Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun and Venus table cells begin in PDF613; Mercury and Moon begin in PDF614. Venus continues from the original PDF613 page bottom, not a second duplicate.
Jupiter's margin refers to Wind, Stench or Putrefaction but its exact printing needs specialist verification; do not silently add reconstructed extra diagnosis terms.
Mercury's historic word that appears to read Ptisick is uncertain in the original image and is not mapped to an established modern condition.
The Aries zodiac row mixes head/face parts and historic conditions, whereas most other signs list body regions; those distinct semantic fields are retained.
The gender-specific eye laterality for Moon and premodern labels involving reproduction, mental capacity, melancholy and humors are period beliefs and not biological or psychiatric facts.
The 1647 source links whole-life health and mortality to positions of the Sun; no survival, disease incidence, or actual patient medical case data are provided.
The original Sun–Moon negative aphorism has an uncertain aspect glyph; no operator is selected.
Significators above versus below horizon and the source's house disease cross-reference do not provide a clinically verified anatomical method.
Historical reference to second-part page245 is not fully diplomatically compared in this batch; reuse only as unverified bibliographic pointer.
Several paths can allege both good health and illness in one chart, with flexible sign/house/planet selection. No preregistered priority or handling of contradiction.
Source relies on classical humoral diseases, including many obsolete names; modern equivalences are not automatically assumed and require expertise.
Original PDF615 first contains the ending of the unnumbered introduction, then a separate divider and printed CHAP CXXVIII on eye impairment. No eye-chapter substantive text is admitted here.
No completed diplomatic transcription or independent paleographic verification of each historical term. Source images and selective qualified terms preserved.
No person-level health advice, diagnostic inference, birth-time rectification, treatment plan, disability prediction or lifespan forecast is authorized.
